verdict.stance: Neutral / Solid Israeli Systemic Bank with Leaner CET1 Cushion (A-/BBB+)
verdict.summary: Israel's 4th-largest bank posted 9M26 net income of NIS 3.04bn (13.4% adj. ROE) with very clean 0.64% NPLs (189% coverage, 16bp CoR) and 121.6% LCR. Mercantile Bank integration is expected to yield ~NIS 250m annual savings, though 10.32% CET1 is leaner than Leumi (11.38%) ahead of 2026-2027 bank tax levies and Jan-28 $800m maturity.

positives: Benign asset quality: NPL ratio improved to 0.64% (189% coverage) with Q3 credit loss expense of just 16bp.
Cost synergy catalyst: Mercantile Bank operational streamlining & workforce program targeting ~NIS 250m annual savings.
Solid liquidity (LCR 121.6%, NSFR 110.4%) and AA- Fitch-rated covered bond framework.
negatives: Thinner capital buffer than peers: CET1 10.32% (vs 9.21% BoI floor) and Total CAR 13.12% alongside 40% dividend payout.
Sovereign/geopolitical linkage and special Israeli bank taxes for 2026-2027.
NII compression from BoI rate easing and domestic deposit competition (Q3 NII NIS 2.44bn vs 2.65bn prior year).

background.business_overview: Israel's fourth-largest commercial bank operating retail, corporate, and SME banking plus US subsidiary IDB Bank NY (~$14.4bn assets).
background.asset_perimeter: Discount Bank Israel, Mercantile Discount Bank (integrating), CAL credit cards (divestment/perimeter tracking), and IDB Bank NY.
background.ownership_governance: Widely held on TASE (DSCT); D-SIB regulated by Bank of Israel.

recent_drivers: Nov-26 (Q3/9M26): 9M NPAT NIS 3.04bn (11.8% ROE / 13.4% adj.), Q3 NPAT NIS 910m (NIS 1.04bn ex-merger charges), NPL 0.64%, CET1 10.32%, CAR 13.12%.
2026: Advancing Mercantile Bank restructuring (~NIS 250m run-rate savings); rating outlooks stabilized to Stable.
